newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures close down, weak cash cited.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures close down, weak cash cited.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended lower Thursday in lackluster trading, following weakness in cash prices, market sources said.
"It was a pretty dismal day. Only about 600 lots traded," said one dealer.
He did note a surge of activity in the Sep-Oct Palo Verde (PV) spread, which widened slightly on the day.
Next-day cash PV traded mostly in the low $30's per megawatt hour, with some late deals reported in the high $20's.
Traders attributed the softness to expected moderate weather conditions over the next several days.
They also expected seasonal factors, including tapering off of hydroelectric power generation, to narrow the spread between PV and California-Oregon border (COB) futures prices.
"COB should start to strengthen against PV, but we will have to see," said a trader.
The September PV contract settled 55 cents lower at $28.63 per megawatt hour (MWh), off its high for the day of $29.60.
October PV lost 30 cents to settle at $21.95 and the November contract fell 15 cents to close at $21.80.
COB futures for September fell 41 cents to close at $22.09, compared with a daily high of $22.60 and a low of $22.00.
The October COB contract lost 20 cents to close at $21.20, while November fell 20 cents to $22.30.
As of 1525 EDT, 168 COB and 459 PV contracts were traded, NYMEX said.
Confirmation that the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power complex in New Mexico would restart in time for Monday's peak also weighed down PV futures, market sources said.
Arizona Public Service Co said Four Corners unit 5 is expected to resume operation sometime Sunday after being shut earlier this month for repairs.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired power plant in Wyoming was scheduled for return to service by Friday.
The 254 MW unit 1 at the Valmy coal-fired power plant in Nevada was expected to restart Sunday or Monday after being shut earlier this week due to a rotor problem.

In their six to 10 day forecasts, meteorologists called for cool, fair weather in the Pacific Northwest. But clouds and tropical moisture were expected to keep temperatures in the Southwest below normal through the weekend, followed by more seasonal weather next week.
Transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern Califoria, remained at 6,300 MW pending final approval of system operating procedures.
Once those are cleared, which is expected to happen by Monday, the rating will be lifted to 6,900 MW.
((--D Beasley, Los Angeles bureau +1 213 955 6761))
